title: Recovery — Band-Assisted Full Body
subtitle: Light resistance-band mobility and activation
coaching_note: This is a lighter, active recovery day — the band adds just enough tension to wake muscles up without adding real fatigue. If anything pinches or sharp-hurts, stop that exercise, don't push through it.

exercises.name: Band Pull-Apart
exercises.form_cue: Arms straight out in front, pull the band apart until it touches your chest, squeeze your shoulder blades together.
exercises.why: Wakes up the mid-back muscles that counter all the forward-rounded posture from sitting and screens.

exercises.name: Band Overhead Pass-Through
exercises.form_cue: Wide grip, arms straight, slowly move the band from in front of your hips to behind your back and back again.
exercises.why: Gently opens shoulder flexion range without any real loading — good for a joint that's tired from training.

exercises.name: Band External Rotation
exercises.form_cue: Elbow bent 90 degrees and pinned to your side, rotate your forearm outward only — the elbow doesn't travel.
exercises.why: Activates the rotator cuff — the small stabilizers that protect the shoulder and are easy to neglect.

exercises.name: Band Lateral Walk
exercises.form_cue: Band around your ankles or just above the knees, slight squat, step sideways keeping tension on the band the whole time.
exercises.why: Activates the glute medius — a muscle that quietly controls knee tracking and is easy to leave undertrained.

exercises.name: Band Monster Walk (forward)
exercises.form_cue: Band above the knees, slight squat, small forward steps keeping tension on the band throughout.
exercises.why: Reinforces the same glute activation pattern in a different plane — good general hip prep.

exercises.name: Seated Band Hamstring Stretch
exercises.form_cue: Lying on your back, loop the band around one foot, straighten the leg toward the ceiling, keep your lower back flat.
exercises.why: Gives you a gentle assisted stretch with more control over the angle than a standing version.

exercises.name: Standing Forward Fold
exercises.form_cue: Soft knees, let your head and arms hang heavy, breathe slow.
exercises.why: Decompresses the spine and brings your heart rate all the way back down.

progression_notes: If glute activation exercises feel like nothing after a few weeks, move to a heavier band rather than adding more reps.
